threads.body: [General] Pekko's `SystemMessageDelivery` sends system messages through `OutboundEnvelope.copy()`. That method creates a new reusable envelope by calling `init` on the Artery stream thread, so this advice overwrites the captured sender context with that thread's root context and the copied envelope is serialized without propagation metadata. Instrument `copy()` and transfer `OUTBOUND_ENVELOPE_CONTEXT` from the original envelope to the returned envelope; add a remote-system-message regression test.
New instrumentation modules also need a row in `docs/supported-libraries.md`, and `Apache Pekko Remote` is missing. The propagation-only `Apache Pekko Actors` row shows the format.

threads.body: [Testing] `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` gives the Artery and classic subclasses separate base instances, but these fields collapse both fixtures into one JVM-wide slot. Keep only `testing` static and make the transport fixture and send/latch state instance-owned, as required for shared abstract test bases.

[General] Appending this field unconditionally can make classic remoting drop an otherwise valid message. `EndpointWriter.writeSend` compares the returned PDU size with `transport.maximumPayloadBytes` and discards oversized PDUs, so a message that previously fit but has less headroom than the propagation field will no longer be delivered when the agent is enabled. Please skip the metadata when it would exceed the transport limit (likely at a point where that limit is available) and cover this boundary case.

[Testing] Nothing exercises the declared `pekko-remote_3` support. This instrumentation matches Scala implementation methods by name, which muzzle does not verify; please reuse these Java tests in a `scala3Test` suite and wire it into `check`, as `pekko-actor-1.0` and `pekko-http-1.0` do.

replies.body:
Added in 7e21785c63: a `scala3Test` suite that runs the same Java tests against the `_3` artifacts, wired into `check`, following `pekko-actor-1.0` and `pekko-http-1.0`. I checked it resolves `pekko-remote_3` and `scala3-library_3` rather than silently falling back to `_2.12`.

It passes 7/7, so the matchers here do hold under scala 3.

Worth saying this was not a theoretical ask. The same point on #19829 turned out to be a live bug: scala 3 compiles the forwarders a class inherits from a trait as bridge methods, ByteBuddy does not advise bridge methods, and the advice there silently never ran. Only the scala 3 suite caught it.

threads.body: [General] Pekko 1.0.0 invokes `PekkoPduProtobufCodec$$`; `PekkoPduProtobufCodec$` is only its static-forwarder mirror in that release, so this advice never runs although the module declares 1.0+. Please match and test the 1.0.0 binary name too, or raise the supported minimum to 1.0.1.

replies.body:
The finding is right. In `pekko-remote_2.13:1.0.0` the object is `PekkoPduProtobufCodec$$` (it has `MODULE$` and implements `PekkoPduCodec`) and `PekkoPduProtobufCodec$` has neither, it only carries the static forwarders. `EndpointWriter` calls `constructMessage` with `invokeinterface`, so the advice does not run on 1.0.0. From 1.0.1 on, `PekkoPduProtobufCodec$` is the object.

I am not adding the 1.0.0 name though. 1.0.1 is the minimum this library builds against for pekko, `pekko-actor-1.0` and `pekko-remote-1.0` both declare `library("org.apache.pekko:pekko-...:1.0.1")`, so 1.0.0 is not a version we support in practice.

I have left the muzzle range at `[1.0,)` to match `pekko-actor-1.0` and `pekko-http-1.0` rather than move this one module to `[1.0.1,)`. Happy to tighten all of them if you would rather the declared range matched the real minimum.

threads.body: [Testing] A probe that arrives after its two-second timeout counts down whichever latch the next probe installed. This can make the test pass when the final context-bearing message was dropped. Correlate each message with its own latch.

replies.body:
Fixed in 8e3f320fd9. Every probe message now starts with a unique `probe-N:` id, the latches live in a map keyed by that id, and the actor only counts down the latch of the probe that sent the message it received. A message that arrives after its two second timeout now counts against its own dead probe rather than the next one, so the binary search cannot mis-measure and the final context-bearing send can only be satisfied by its own message.

The id takes up part of the requested size instead of adding to it, which keeps the measured frame limit honest; the sizes probed near the limit are far larger than the id.

threads.body:
[General] This module also registers classic remoting, so the Artery-only description omits half of its behavior.
```suggestion
/**
 * Propagates context with remote messages sent between Pekko cluster nodes. Artery uses the
 * {@code RemoteInstrument} SPI, while classic remoting appends an unknown protobuf field. The
 * received context is restored before dispatch so Pekko actor instrumentation can carry it to the
 * receiving actor.
 */
```

In https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/main/instrumentation/rmi/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/rmi/context/ContextPayload.java and https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/main/instrumentation/thrift-0.13/library/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/thrift/v0_13/internal/ContextPropagationUtil.java we limit the number of context entires to 100 and the size to 8k chars

replies.body:
Added in 8e3f320fd9, with the same limits and FINE logging as the rmi `ContextPayload`: writing skips propagation above 100 entries, and reading rejects more than 100 entries or more than 8k chars. The existing 4k byte cap stays as well, that one is about not eating into the artery frame rather than about trust.

Doing this surfaced a real hole on the read side: `readString` allocated `new byte[buffer.getShort()]`, so a corrupt or hostile negative length threw `NegativeArraySizeException`, which is not in `ProtobufContext.decode`'s catch list and would have escaped the artery `RemoteInstrument` callback with no catch of ours at all. Every length prefix is now validated against the bytes that remain, and anything that does not fit is reported as no context.

threads.body: If the classic and artery instrumentations are independent could also consider having them in separate instrumentation modules. Then you wouldn't need `ArteryInstrumentations` and `ClassicInstrumentations`. This would also avoid muzzle failing when only one of these implementations is present, idk whether it is possible to exclude one of these. Though this is fine too.

replies.body: I'd keep the single module. The scenario the split would guard against cannot arise here: artery and classic remoting both live in the `pekko-remote` artifact itself (the classic codec and `EndpointWriter` included, only the netty transport dependency is external), so muzzle never sees one implementation without the other. Splitting would trade the two grouping classes for a second module's worth of boilerplate without changing what can match. Happy to revisit if pekko ever separates the artifacts.

threads.body: [General] Capping the metadata itself at 4 KiB does not preserve Artery message delivery. Pekko writes this metadata into the fixed-capacity `EnvelopeBuffer` before writing the actor refs, manifest, and message; if those later writes overflow, Pekko drops the whole message. Consequently, a payload that fits without the agent but has less headroom than this metadata becomes undeliverable. Please make Artery retry/serialize without this metadata when it consumes the message's remaining frame space, and cover the near-frame-limit case as the classic transport test does.

replies.body:
The mechanism described here is real, I verified it in `Codecs.scala`: the encoder writes the instrument metadata into the envelope buffer before the payload is serialized, and on `BufferOverflowException` it publishes `Dropped` with no retry. But the remedy does not exist at the level this code runs at, and the difference from the classic transport is worth spelling out.

In classic remoting our advice runs in `constructMessage` after the message is serialized, with `transport.maximumPayloadBytes` in hand, so "skip the metadata when it will not fit" was computable and that is what the earlier fix does. In artery, `remoteWriteMetadata` is called before the payload exists; the remaining frame space is unknowable from inside the `RemoteInstrument` SPI. A retry without metadata would mean instrumenting artery's `Encoder` catch block to re-run serialization, and serializing a message twice is not safe to assume side effect free.

This property is inherent to the SPI rather than to this instrument: kamon's `RemoteInstrument` and pekko's own carry it too, and pekko's designed answer is operational, `LoggingRemoteInstrument` with `log-frame-size-exceeding` exists precisely so operators size `maximum-frame-size` with instrument overhead in mind. The 4k cap bounds the exposure to about 1.5% of the default 256 KiB artery frame, and a typical traceparent plus tracestate is around a hundred bytes.

So I am leaving artery as is unless a maintainer would like the encoder instrumented; happy to discuss what that would take.
